dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation

evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py, filter.json; sampled c-testsuite tests 00001-00010 and explored wacc chapter structure/expected_results before coding — establishes basic test-suite orientation (anchor 5).
Checked rustc/cargo/gcc versions but got no output; never followed up with systematic ABI reference-case probing — ABI conventions were assumed rather than investigated.
Used gcc -c on generated assembly to detect assembler-rejected constructs; ABI/register-width/alignment issues discovered reactively via assembler errors rather than proactive probing.
Root-caused register-width and format-string ABI bugs only after assembler failures — evidence the calling-convention/assembly contract was recovered reactively, not up front.

Continually mined individual failing tests to infer needed semantics (function-like macros, variadic, sizeof decay, chained assignment) — sustained but shallow, one-test-at-a-time, without systematic feature categorization.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's opening orientation squarely matches anchor 5: it read the test harness and sampled each suite before establishing the basic emit-assembly/gcc-link path and calling convention. It falls short of anchor 8 because it never systematically categorized tests by feature/difficulty up front, never extracted an explicit language subset, and probed ABI edge cases only reactively (fixing register widths, alignment, and relocation-style issues after assembler rejections rather than by compiling reference cases). Its later, reactive mining of failing tests to infer semantics adds a touch of higher-anchor flavor but is shallow and one-test-at-a-time, so the observed level sits at 5.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure

evidence.note: Initial plans lay out a clear, dependency-reasonable module ordering (token→lexer→ast→preprocessor→parser→sema→codegen→main), but only at the pass/module level — no feature milestones or explicit completion criteria are defined.

Agent wrote all compiler modules up front in one push before any test ran, then spent ~80 steps just getting a clean build. This is a big-bang approach rather than smallest-viable-slice staging with per-feature done-checks.
Debug phase is organized as reactive bug-by-bug fixing; plans repeatedly say 'identify next most impactful bug pattern' — impact-aware but not a structured feature roadmap tied to test subsets.

Late in the run the agent breaks results down by suite (c_testsuite 54%, wacc 61%, gcc_torture 15%) and decides to 'focus on these standard C tests first' — genuine data-driven prioritization, but arriving only near the end and at triage level, not as a pre-planned milestone hierarchy.
Ending 'Plan' fields remain tactical next-bug lists; no milestone hierarchy with gating criteria ever materialized across the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent established a clear pass structure in a reasonable dependency order and loosely tied its work to getting tests passing, with some late impact-based prioritization by suite — matching parts of anchor 5. But it never defined feature-level milestones with concrete test-subset done-signals, and its approach was build-everything-then-debug (big-bang) rather than dependency-ordered smallest-viable slices, keeping it below anchor 5 and well short of the fine-grained, gated milestone structure of anchor 8. This places observed behavior between the 'vague ordering' (3) and 'clear roadmap with loosely-tied milestones' (5) anchors, at a 4.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design

evidence.note: Before writing code, reads run_tests.sh/py, filter.json, expected_results.json and many individual test .c files to understand the pass/fail signal and required features — establishing what verification will measure.

Adds a -S flag specifically to emit assembly, then reads generated asm for failing test 00100.c to localize concrete codegen bugs (double epilogue, reversed subtraction, _start conflict) rather than assuming correctness.

Compiles single failing test 00004.c to assembly, spots 'movl (%rax), %rax' width mismatch, reasons about what correct output should be (%eax), and fixes the specific load path — root-cause isolation to the codegen pass.
Runs batch loops over targeted test-ID subsets (e.g. 00083-00088) and distinguishes defect categories (function-like macros = preprocessor, variadic = parser, asm syntax = codegen) to guide fixes.

Tracks per-suite pass breakdown (c_testsuite 79/146, wacc 135/221, gcc_torture 63/413) from existing runner output to prioritize the most tractable failures — but relies on the handed-over runner, with no regression guards (score oscillated 262→294→277).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently goes beyond the level-5 pattern: it doesn't just run subsets and read pass/fail, it reduces to individual failing tests, adds an assembly-dump flag, inspects generated asm, and reasons about what correct output should look like to pinpoint the buggy pass (lexer/parser/sema/codegen) — clear level-8 behaviors sustained across the whole trajectory. It falls short of a full 8/10 because it uses whole existing test files as repros rather than crafting minimal cases, never diffs against a known-correct reference (gcc -S), and builds no verification infrastructure or regression guards beyond the handed-over runner, despite visible score regressions. This places it solidly at 7.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection

evidence.note: Runs the full 780-test suite repeatedly and records a running tally with percentages (11.2% → 13.6% → 15.9% → 26.8%), consistently attributing each jump to specific fixes (register widths, shift ops, division). Clear whole-suite scoreboard maintained throughout.

Maintains per-suite breakdown (c_testsuite 79/146, wacc 135/221, gcc_torture 63/413) and uses it to prioritize — explicitly picks c-testsuite as 'most tractable' standard-C work. Continuously re-derives highest-leverage work from the scoreboard.

Detects a regression (294→277) and correctly attributes it: 'Score dropped from 294 to 277 between runs, indicating recent parser edits may have introduced regressions.' Strong, immediate regression detection with attribution — a level-10 behavior.

Loops repeatedly on a single stubborn test (nested -> member access), re-diagnosing it inconsistently as 'ternary operator' then 'nested member access' across many steps, without ever bounding effort and decisively moving on. This is circular debugging it recognized only weakly.

Recurring state-tracking confusion about whether builds actually applied ('binary is cached', 'score unchanged despite rewrite — may be using cached binary'), forcing cargo clean rebuilds — indicates imperfect done-vs-remaining bookkeeping.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps a solid running tally of pass counts by suite/feature and clearly notices regressions — it caught the 294→277 drop and attributed it to parser edits, a hallmark of the top anchors. This exceeds level 5. However it falls short of level 8's 'bounds effort and moves on rather than looping': it circled on 00019.c ~29 times with inconsistent re-diagnoses and never deliberately abandoned it, and repeatedly lost track of whether builds applied (cached-binary confusion). Strong regression tracking and scoreboard-driven prioritization pull it above 5, but the unbroken looping and state-tracking slips keep it below 8.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognized that codegen's ld()/register-width handling (returning %rax for all sizes) was structurally wrong for type-aware sized ops; reworked the load/store width scheme (ld()/rw(), %eax vs %rax) and re-ran the full suite to confirm gains (11%→~27%). Genuine component rework + re-verify = level-5 behavior.

Diagnosed stack-alignment overlap for negative offsets as a real data-layout bug, switched to div_euclid/rem_euclid floor division, and re-verified against the segfaulting pointer test. Targeted correction rather than a local hack.

Judged the preprocessor #if evaluator 'too basic' (only handled defined/single ident) and deliberately rewrote it as a proper recursive-descent expression parser, then rebuilt/re-tested. Component-level rework of a falsified approach.

Recognized the limitation as ARCHITECTURAL — type information lost through codegen for self-referential/incomplete structs, needing type tracking threaded through sema/codegen (approaching level 8 recognition). But the resolve_type refactor had compile errors, was removed (426), re-added to codegen, and 'apparently didn't help'; nested -> member access stayed broken. The architectural refactor was never landed or confirmed to unblock the feature, so it falls short of the level-8 anchor.

Much of the 'rewrite from scratch' activity is recovery from self-inflicted sed corruption ('going around in circles with sed corrupting files'), i.e. firefighting/thrash rather than design falsification — this does not constitute adaptation and caps the score.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly reworks failing components (register widths, alignment, preprocessor #if) and re-verifies with test runs, cleanly matching the level-5 anchor. It also once recognizes an architectural limitation (type info lost through codegen for incomplete structs) and attempts to thread type resolution through sema/codegen — reaching toward level 8 in recognition — but the refactor is never successfully executed or confirmed to unblock the stuck feature class, and a large share of its 'rewrites' are recovery from self-inflicted sed corruption rather than genuine design correction. This lands solidly at 5: reworks-and-reverifies is demonstrated, but the deliberate architectural refactor that defines level 8 is attempted and abandoned, not achieved.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight

evidence.note: Upfront deliberate module separation (token/lexer/ast/preprocessor/parser/sema/codegen) and a type-aware AST with Type::Func, Struct/Union (name,fields,size,align), pointers, arrays — showing intent toward a type/layout model beyond the trivial.

Core representation choices were internally inconsistent and only caught at compile time (Struct/Union field-count mismatch, Type::Func param-type shape, analyze_expr Expr vs Box<Expr>), indicating the initial design was not carefully specified.
Parser, sema, and codegen were rewritten wholesale from scratch repeatedly — the opposite of features slotting in additively, contradicting the level-8 anchor.

Later hard features (array decay, designated initializers, nested -> member chains, incomplete-type resolution) exposed representation gaps; nested member access was never solved because intermediate-type threading wasn't in the design.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent achieved the level-5 anchor solidly — clean lexer/parser/sema/codegen separation with type/scope/layout data structures — and even reached toward the type/layout model implied by level 8. But the design was not robust: it required numerous wholesale rewrites of the parser, sema, and codegen, and later hard features (nested struct access, incomplete types, designated initializers) exposed gaps rather than slotting in cleanly, which is exactly what the level-8 anchor rules out. That places the observed behavior at the clean-separation level with only partial foresight, i.e. a 5.

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a from-scratch C compiler in Rust spanning lexer, full preprocessor, parser, semantic analysis, and x86-64 codegen, plus many advanced features (structs/unions, switch/case, typedef/casts, globals, short-circuit eval), gated by 780 tests across three real-world suites that must all pass. Difficulty comes from sheer scope, deep interdependence between passes, an implicit contract (C semantics + x86-64 ABI) the agent must recover, and the near-certainty that naive early design decisions will break under later features. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in every meta-work faculty — deep orientation, staged milestones tied to test subsets, relentless test-driven verification, accurate pass-rate tracking, and willingness to refactor architecture mid-flight.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI & test-suite orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C language semantics, the x86-64 System V ABI/assembly conventions, and the structure/content of the three test suites before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 'spec' is largely implicit — correct behavior is defined by C semantics, the calling convention, and what the 780 tests actually exercise. Acting without recovering this contract guarantees rework across nearly every pass.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of the test suites, run_tests.sh, or ABI conventions; guesses at behavior.
anchors.3: Skims run_tests.sh and writes a trivial hello-world compile; no systematic look at what features the tests demand or how the ABI/relocation works.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh, samples tests from each suite, and establishes the basic x86-64 calling convention and assembly emission path before building core codegen.
anchors.8: Systematically categorizes tests by feature/difficulty, extracts the concrete language subset required, and probes ABI edge cases (struct passing, sizes/alignment, relocations) by compiling small reference cases; orientation directly shapes the build order.
anchors.10: Sustained, iterative research: continually mines failing tests to infer exact semantic requirements (integer promotion, evaluation order, layout rules), verifies assumptions against the assembler/linker behavior, and maintains a living understanding of the target contract that anticipates features before they are reached.

dimensions.name: Feature staging & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered hierarchy of passes and feature milestones, each with an explicit done-check (e.g. a passing test subset).
dimensions.why_it_matters: You cannot build all of C at once; the difference between steady progress and thrashing is a sane dependency-ordered plan (expressions before control flow before types before structs) with checkpoints.

anchors.0: No decomposition; attempts the whole compiler as one undifferentiated push or jumps between unrelated features at random.
anchors.3: Vague ordering ('do lexer, then parser, then codegen') with no feature-level milestones or explicit completion criteria.
anchors.5: Clear pass structure plus a feature roadmap in a reasonable dependency order, with milestones loosely tied to getting some tests passing.
anchors.8: Fine-grained, dependency-aware milestones each bound to a concrete test subset as its done-signal, sequenced so each milestone builds on verified prior ones; ordering reflects which features unlock the most tests.
anchors.10: A living milestone hierarchy that is re-prioritized as data arrives — smallest-viable-slice ordering, explicit gating criteria per milestone, and deliberate deferral of hard/rare features until foundations are proven, sustained coherently across the whole horizon.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building/using checks — incremental runs of test subsets, minimal repro cases, diffing against expected behavior — rather than assuming generated code is correct.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 opaque pass/fail tests and a compiler where any pass can silently miscompile, a disciplined verification loop is the only way to know progress is real and to localize defects.

anchors.0: Never runs the tests until the very end, or writes code with no way to confirm correctness; assumes success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as the only check; no isolation of failures, no smaller probes.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets after each feature and uses the pass/fail signal to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Builds a tight loop: reduces failing tests to minimal reproductions, inspects generated assembly, and compares against known-correct output to pinpoint which pass is wrong before editing.
anchors.10: Engineers verification infrastructure beyond what's handed over — categorized/scriptable subset runs, regression guards so fixed tests stay fixed, and root-cause isolation that distinguishes lexer/parser/sema/codegen defects — sustaining fast, trustworthy signal across the entire build.

dimensions.name: Pass-rate tracking & thrash detection
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture (which tests/features pass), and detecting regressions, circular debugging, or stalls across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Over hundreds of features and edits, it is easy to lose the plot, regress previously-passing tests, or loop on one stubborn failure; an accurate live picture is what sustains net forward motion.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which features remain; edits blindly with no scoreboard.
anchors.3: Occasional whole-suite counts but no tracking of trends, regressions, or which categories are outstanding.
anchors.5: Keeps a running tally of pass counts by suite/feature and notices when a change breaks previously-passing tests.
anchors.8: Maintains a structured, current view of pass rate by category and remaining work, and recognizes when stuck on one test — bounding effort and moving on rather than looping.
anchors.10: Treats pass-rate as a managed signal: detects regressions immediately and attributes them, spots circular/thrashing debugging early and deliberately changes tactics, and continuously re-derives the highest-leverage remaining work from the scoreboard.

dimensions.name: Design revision under falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, data structures, or approach when a later feature (types, structs, ABI detail) exposes that an earlier design cannot support it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compilers are notorious for early choices (untyped AST, ad-hoc register allocation, string-based codegen) that collapse under types/structs; the ability to recognize and refactor rather than pile hacks decides whether the tail of the task is reachable.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a broken design, piling special-cases and hacks even as failures compound.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally; resists structural change even when the same class of bug keeps recurring.
anchors.5: When an approach clearly fails, reworks the affected component and re-verifies rather than forcing it.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a limitation is architectural (not local), makes a deliberate refactor (e.g. adding type info through the AST/IR), and confirms the change unblocks the stuck feature class.
anchors.10: Proactively detects design strain before it becomes a wall, weighs refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, executes larger restructurings cleanly while protecting already-passing tests, and updates the plan/design record so the correction propagates instead of recurring.

dimensions.name: Compiler architecture & IR foresight
dimensions.description: Choosing pass boundaries and core data structures (AST/IR, symbol tables, type representation) with enough foresight to accommodate the full required feature set rather than painting into a corner.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike generic decomposition (what to do when) or adaptation (fixing after breakage), this is the upfront design judgment specific to compilers: a representation that anticipates types, structs, and the ABI avoids the most expensive class of rework on this task.

anchors.0: No deliberate architecture; monolithic, ad-hoc string-munging with no separable passes or reusable structures.
anchors.3: Minimal structure that works for the first trivial cases but has no provision for types, scopes, or layout.
anchors.5: Clean separation of lexer/parser/sema/codegen with data structures adequate for the early feature milestones.
anchors.8: Core representations (typed AST/IR, symbol/scope tables, type/layout model) are designed with the later hard features in mind, so structs/typedef/switch slot in without wholesale rewrites.
anchors.10: Architecture demonstrably anticipates the full contract — extensible IR and type system, clear invariants between passes — enabling most advanced features to be added additively; foresight is evidenced by later features landing cleanly rather than by luck.
